7  Non-Safety-Related with Special Treatment Structure, System, and Component Criteria and
Capabilities

This chapter of the safety evaluation (SE) summarizes the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission
(NRC) staffs review and evaluation of the Long Mott Generating Station (LMGS) preliminary
safety analysis report (PSAR) chapter 7, “Non-Safety-Related with Special Treatment Structure,
System, and Component Criteria and Capabilities.”

7.1 Reliability and Capability Targets for Non-Safety-Related with Special Treatment
Structures, Systems, and Components

PSAR section 7.1 describes the applicant's approach to developing reliability and capability
targets for non-safety-related with special treatment (NSRST) structures, systems, or
components (SSCs) and presents the set of targets developed based on the preliminary design.

The applicable regulatory requirements for the evaluation of Reliability and Capability Targets
for NSRST SSCs are as follows:

e 50.34(a)(4)
e 50.35(a)(1)

The applicable guidance for the review of PSAR section 7.1 is as follows:

e Regulatory Guide (RG) 1.233, Revision 0, “Guidance for a Technology Inclusive, Risk-
Informed, and Performance-Based Methodology to Inform the Licensing Basis and
Content of Applications for Licenses, Certifications, and Approvals for Non-Light-Water
Reactors,” (ML20091L698), which endorses with clarifications, the guidance in NEI 18-
04, Revision 1, “Risk-Informed Performance-Based Technology Inclusive Guidance for
Non-Light Water Reactor Licensing Basis Development,” (ML19241A472).

e RG 1.253, Revision 0, “Guidance for a Technology-Inclusive Content of Application
Methodology to Inform the Licensing Basis and Content of Applications for Licenses,
Certifications, and Approvals for Non-Light-Water Reactors,” which endorses with
clarifications and additions NEI 21-07, Revision 1, “Technology Inclusive Guidance for
Non-Light Water Reactor Safety Analysis Report: For Applicants Utilizing NEI 18-04
Methodology” (ML22060A190).

7.1.1. Technical Evaluation

 OFFICIALUSE- ONLY _PROPRIETARYINFORMATHON

As described in PSAR section 1.3.1, the applicant is implementing the LMP methodology as
outlined in RG 1.233, which endorses NEI 18-04. NEI 18-04 contains guidance on defining the
reliability and capability targets as part of the LMP methodology. As described in PSAR chapter
1, “General Plant and Site Description and Overview of Licensing Basis,” LME is generally
following the content and organization guidance provided in NEI 21-07 and endorsed with
clarifications in RG 1.253. NEI 21-07, Revision 1, section C.7.1, “Reliability and Capability
Targets for NSRST SSCs,” contains applicable guidance for content and review of this section
of the PSAR.

The NRC staff evaluated this PSAR section using the guidance in RG 1.233 and RG 1.253. As
described in NEI 18-04, reliability and capability targets are used to establish controls on the
frequency and consequence levels of non-design basis accident (DBA) licensing basis events
(LBEs) and to inform the selection of special treatment requirements for safety-related (SR) and
NSRST SSCs. LME provides preliminary plant-level reliability and capability targets for NSRST
SSCs in PSAR table 7.1-1 to meet the plant-level safety objectives. The reliability and capability
targets established ensure that the design supports the inputs and assumptions used by the
safety analysis and to support staff findings for 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) and 50.35(a)(1).

The preliminary targets provided in the PSAR are limited to NSRST PSFs that are explicitly
modeled in the probabilistic risk assessment (PRA) used to support the PSAR. As described in
section 3.1.1 of this SE, the scope of this PRA is limited to at-power internal events for the
reactor and some SSCs are not modeled within the construction permit (CP) stage PRA. The
NRC staff determined that limiting the preliminary reliability and capability targets based on the
PRA scope is sufficient for the CP application given the preliminary design stage, the additional
PRA development that will occur between the CP and the operating license (OL), and LME’s
commitment to follow the guidance in the NEI 18-04 methodology which includes defining
reliability and capability targets for all safety-significant SSCs.

PSAR table 7.1-1, “Reliability and Capability Targets for NSRST,” defines the preliminary
reliability and capability targets for the following 13 unique NSRST PRA safety functions (PSFs):

e NSRST PSF 2.7.3: Control the frequency of large depressurization events

Two NSRST PSFs are listed twice in the table, PSF 1.2.2.2 and PSF 1.2.2.2.3, to capture
unique capability targets related to achieving the PSF. As the PRA, safety analysis, and the
associated reliability and capability targets continue to develop these may be assigned distinct
PSFs and the SSCs they are associated with will be identified and documented. Based on the
preliminary nature of the PRA and design, the staff determined the approach of capturing
multiple aspects of a function under one PSF was reasonable for the CP stage.

PSAR table 7.1-1 does not include the functions of some NSRST SSCs, classified as NSRST
based on providing a load path for SR SSCs. This approach to classification is inconsistent with
the methodology in NEI 18-04 and LME has provided their justification for this deviation in
section 5.1 of the PSAR. The reliability and capability targets for these SSCs will be determined
through their structural and seismic design requirements and the adequacy of these targets to
support the overall safety analysis will be confirmed through the seismic PRA, as discussed in
PSAR section 3.7 and evaluated in section 3.7.1 of this SE.

PSAR table 7.1-1, defines the reliability targets to be the following three for the majority of the
NSRST PSFs listed:

e Maintain frequency of all LBEs with failure of this PSF below 1E-2 per plant year.
e Maintain LBEs with failure of this NSRST PSF within the F-C target.
e Maintain cumulative risk metrics within targets.

However, the reliability targets for NSRST PSFs 1.3.2.1, 2.2.1, 2.7.1, and 2.7.2 are:

e Maintain LBEs with failure of this NSRST PSF within the F-C target.
e Maintain cumulative risk metrics within targets.

During the regulatory audit (MLXXXXXXxX), LME stated that, for NSRST PSFs 1.3.2.1, 2.7.1,
and 2.7.2 the reliability target “Maintain frequency of all LBEs with failure of this PSF below 1E-2
per plant year’ is not used because the NSRST PSF classification is based on the judgment of
the integrated decision-making process panel (IDPP), and that for NSRST PSF 2.2.1 the
reliability target is not used because PSF 2.2.1 is classified as NSRST due to risk significance.
Although the applicant did not explain why the plant level frequency target in question would not
apply to these PSFs, the NRC staff determined that based on the preliminary design stage and
the commitment to provide system level reliability targets at the OL application stage that further
review of the frequency targets for these PSFs could be left to the OL without undue risk to the
health and safety of the public.

The applicant stated that the basis for the functional-level reliability targets is derived from the
development of the frequency targets for a collection of LBEs that are prevented or mitigated by
a particular NSRST. However, the reliability targets listed above from PSAR table 7.1-1 align
with the overall requirements that the plant must meet, without further definition of the reliability
various functions will need to achieve. Therefore, because the reliability targets align with the
overall requirements, the NRC staff determined that the preliminary reliability targets defined are
aligned with plant level targets, as defined in section 6.2 of NEI 21-07.

 NEI 21-07 states that reliability and capability targets can be established at different levels; plant
level, functional level, or SSC level. Thus, the applicant’s approach of establishing plant-level
targets at the CP stage with a defined methodology for establishing functional and SSC-level
targets at the OL stage is consistent with RG 1.253, which endorses NEI 21-07. The plant-level
targets are discussed in PSAR chapter 3, “Methodologies, Analyses, and Licensing Basis
Events,” and chapter 4, “Integrated Evaluations,” associated with the frequency-consequence
target and cumulative risk metrics.

The LME process for developing functional and system-level reliability targets from the plant
level targets is described in PSAR section 6.2. This process involves associating the functions
with the LBEs they impact and then optimizing the set as a whole to determine the frequency
target for each function that maximizes margin between the PRA modeled performance and the
target performance impacting the conclusions of the safety analysis. The results from exercising
this method for setting reliability targets will be evaluated at the OL application stage consistent
with NEI 21-07.

The applicant also proposed a capability target for each PSF identified in PSAR table 7.1-1. The
PSAR states that the capability target is informed by the success criteria used in the PRA to
determine success or failure of a particular NSRST PSF at the functional level and aligns with
the corresponding reliability target.

The NRC staff reviewed the proposed preliminary reliability and capability targets and
determined them to be reasonable and acceptable based on the following:

1. The preliminary reliability and capability targets for the NSRST PSFs and associated
SSCs support the overall plant-level objectives discussed in the PSAR.

2. Defining plant-level and functional-level targets, instead of SSC-level targets, at the CP
stage is reasonable because of the preliminary nature of the LMGS design

7.1.2 Conclusion

Based on its review, the NRC staff finds that the information on the reliability and capability
targets for NSRST SSCs, described in PSAR Section 7.1, is consistent with the applicable
regulatory guidance and meets the regulatory requirements in under 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) and 10
CFR 50.35(a)(1).

7.2 Special Treatment Requirements for NSRST SSCs

PSAR section 7.2 describes the applicant’s approach to selecting special treatment
requirements for NSRST SSCs. Special treatment requirements as defined in NEI 18-04
and stated in PSAR section 7.2 are, “requirements that provide increased assurance
beyond normal industrial practices that structures, systems, and components (SSCs)
perform their design-basis functions.”

The applicable regulatory requirements for the evaluation of NSRST SSCs are as follows:

7.2.1 Technical Evaluation

RG 1.253, which endorses NEI 21-07 with clarifications, provides applicable guidance in section
C.7.2, “Special Treatment Requirements for NSRST SSCs” for the content and review of PSAR
section 7.2.

PSAR section 7.2 states that the systematic process that LME uses for special treatment
selection will be presented in the FSAR. The systematic process for selecting special treatments
for NSRST SSCs considers the NSRST PRA safety functions (NSRST PSFs) performed by the
SSCs and their associated reliability and capability targets. The integrated decision-making
process panel (IDPP) reviews and approves the selection of special treatments.

The NRC staff evaluated the preliminary process described in the PSAR and supplemented its
understanding through a focused audit engagement. During the focused audit engagement, the
NRC staff and LME engaged in a discussion of how this process is implemented by LME. The
NRC staff was able to confirm through this audit engagement that the preliminary process is
being used to systematically evaluate the special treatments being applied to each system with
NSRST components. The process also includes an IDPP review of design documents prior to a
review meeting which includes representatives from safety, engineering, operations,
maintenance, etc.

A preliminary set of special treatments are described in the SSC descriptions within PSAR
section 7.3. For some NSRST SSCs, nuclear codes and standards have been selected for
design as special treatments. The use of nuclear codes and standards is considered special
treatment in the NEI 18-04 methodology. Additionally, application of the programs described in
chapter 8 of the PSAR (e.g., quality assurance, reliability integrity management, inservice
testing) are also considered special treatments by NEI 18-04. Section 7.3 of this SE, which
includes technical evaluation sections for the NSRST systems and structures, notes where

nuclear codes and standards, design or construction requirements beyond commercial, or
programmatic special treatments were applied by LME as special treatments . Special
treatments for NSRST portions of SR systems are noted in section 6.4 of this SE.

As stated in PSAR section 7.2, the special treatments are derived from the reliability and
capability targets for the SSCs, which consider each SSC’s performance during every
applicable LBE. Based on this statement and the associated description, the staff determined
that the performance targets and special treatments will be consistent with what is being relied
on in the safety analysis. These statements on the alignment with the full scope of LBEs were
identified as necessary based on the limited scope used for the PDCs, CDCs, RFDCs, and
SRDCs, as discussed in section 5.3 of this SE. As additional criteria established to address
inconsistencies between the PDCs and the safety analysis, the reliability and capability targets
and special treatments are principal architectural and engineering criteria for the design under
10 CFR 50.35(a)(1).

A final set of special treatments for NSRST SSCs is expected to be summarized in the FSAR, in
addition to being provided in the corresponding NSRST system subsections.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR section 7.2 against the guidance in NEI 21-07. The preliminary
special treatments described in the subsections of 7.3 are sufficient for the CP stage because
they ensure the systems can perform the NSRST PSFs they are being relied on for, consistent
with the preliminary state of the design. The format and content presented in PSAR table 7.2-1
is consistent with Table 7.1 of NEI 21-07 and provides a reasonable approach to summarize the
special treatments in the FSAR.

7.2.2 Conclusion

The NRC staff reviewed the approach to assigning special treatment requirements to NSRST
SSCs described in PSAR section 7.2 and determined that the approach is acceptable LME is
using a systematic approach that is consistent with the methodology in NEI 18-04, endorsed
with clarification by RG 1.233. This description is sufficient to address the methodology portions
of the associated regulatory requirements under 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) and 10 CFR 50.35(a)(1).

The content of the PSAR is sufficient for the CP stage based on the special treatments
described as part of the preliminary design and the format and content proposed for section 7.2
of the FSAR being reasonable and consistent with the guidance in NEI 21-07, as endorsed with
clarifications in RG 1.253.

7.3.1.1 Technical Evaluation

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR section 7.3.1, which describes NSRST structures identified via
the integrated decision-making process These NSRST structures include:

Fuel handling annex building (FHAB)

Inter-unit access tunnel (IUAT)

Spent fuel intermediate storage facility (SFISF)
Canister processing facility (CPF)

Nuclear island auxiliary structure (NIAS)

For each structure, NRC staff evaluated its safety significance, compliance with applicable
PDCs, and safety functions.

7.3.1.1.1 Fuel Handling Annex Building (FHAB)

The FHAB consists primarily of a structural steel superstructure with a portion of the FHAB
adjacent to the SST (i.e., the entry points into the SST) consisting of precast concrete walls
required for radiation shielding. PSAR figure 7.3.1-1 shows, in part, an elevation view of the
FHAB, showing the structural steel portion of the FHAB and a precast portion of the FHAB. The
figure also shows top of slab elevations for the multiple floor/roof elevations of the FHAB.
Additionally, PSAR figures 7.3.1-2 through 7.3.1-5 show plan views and related dimensions for
multiple elevations of the FHAB. PSAR section 3.7 describes, in part, the analysis and design
criteria and materials applicable to the FHAB.

Safety Significance

As described in PSAR section 7.3.1.1, the FHAB provides operational and maintenance space
for the mechanical and electrical systems located within the building and is used to store,
handle, and load fresh fuel into the FHS. The building houses the FHS, including the remotely
operated special tooling (ROST), reactivity control and shutdown system (RCSS), and reactor
protection system (RPS) cabinet rooms, among others. Further, the building serves as the main
entry point into the reactor bays. PSAR section 5.1.1 addresses safety classification criteria and
the associated basis applicable to the FHAB including the implementation of design and
analysis special treatments that achieve performance levels consistent with the SSCs being
supported/protected by the FHAB. Moreover, per PSAR section 5.5.2 and table 5.5-21, while
not modeled in the PRA at the CP stage, the FHAB is one of the SSCs that were classified as
NSRST for DID adequacy via the integrated decision-making process. PSAR table 5.5-21 and
section 7.3.1.1.1 indicate that the PSF for the FHAB is to prevent excessive challenges to the
fuel and other SR SSCs within the building in response to external hazards due to building
collapse. SE section 5.1.1 provides additional detail on the NRC staff's evaluation of safety
classification.

The NRC staff also reviewed the PSAR for quality assurance treatment applicable to the FHAB.

The NRC staff finds that LME’s preliminary design bases for the FHAB meet the requirements of

conservative determination of demands (e.g., seismic demands), the commercial standards
used are supplemented as necessary with provisions from nuclear codes and standards, and
the FHAB is within the scope of LME’s QA program.
